draft.title: Population-wide initiatives
card: A population-wide initiative aims to raise activity across a whole community or country, not just one person. It reaches many people at once.
an organised activity or campaign, such as a school sport day or a public campaign that encourages walking.
a rule or plan set by a government or organisation, such as a required amount of physical education time in schools.
a built or natural space that makes activity easier, such as bike paths, parks and safe footpaths.
draft.remember: Population-wide initiatives use programs, policies and environments to help many people be active at once.

a.q: Which of these is a population-wide initiative?
opts: A council builds bike paths linking suburbs across a city
A teenager sets a goal to jog three times a week
A coach writes a training plan for one netball player
A person logs their daily steps on a watch
a.why: Bike paths are an environment that can help everyone in a city be active. The other options are aimed at one person, so they are personal choices or plans, not population-wide initiatives.
a.clue: Which one is aimed at a whole community, not one person?

b.q: A state government requires every primary school to timetable a set amount of physical education each week. What type of initiative is this?
opts: A policy, because it is a rule that applies to many schools
A program, because it is an organised public campaign
An environment, because it takes place inside school grounds
A personal plan, because each student takes part in it
b.why: A required amount of physical education is a rule set by a government, so it is a policy. It is tempting to call it an environment because it happens at school, but the initiative is the rule, not the space.
b.clue: Look at what the government is doing: building a space, running an event or setting a rule?

a.best: A council builds bike paths linking suburbs across a city

b.best: A policy, because it is a rule that applies to many schools
